nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَوَآءٌ مِّنْكُمْ مَّنْ أَسَرَّ ٱلْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌ بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-sārib (السَّارب) is the one who is out in the open.
Qatāda said: al-sārib is the one out in the open, the one going about.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ means concealed in acts of disobedience, and «sāribun bi-l-nahār» means out in the open.
Some of the people of language said: ﴿وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ means out in the open, from خَفَيْتُه meaning "I brought it out into the open," and ﴿وَسَارِبٌ بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ means concealed, from their saying: انسرب الوحش, "the wild animal slipped away," when it enters its lair.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting because of the eminence of those who held it, and it is closer to the meaning, because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: equal among you are the one who keeps his speech secret and the one who declares it, the one who hides himself by night and the one who appears by day; all of that is equal in Allah's knowledge.
And it is better known and more common in the language.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says سَرَب يَسْرُب سَرْباً وسُرُوباً when he goes off.
And al-Aṣmaʿī related: خَلِّ له سَرْبَه, i.e. "leave his way clear for him."

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
There are three views on the verse:
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Angels who guard him; then when the decree comes, they leave him to it.
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — he said: by Allah's permission; they are of Allah's command, and they are angels.
Al-Ḥasan said: "by (ʿan) Allah's command."
Mujāhid and Qatāda said — and this is Qatāda's wording —: They are angels who take turns by night and by day by (ʿan) Allah's command, i.e. by Allah's command.
So this is one view.
The second view: it was narrated from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ — he said: They are the rulers who have people in front of them and behind them, guarding them from Allah's command; but when Allah's command comes, they are of no use at all.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: It is the ruler who seeks to guard himself against Allah, and those are the people of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
And Shuʿba narrated from Sharqī, from ʿIkrima, who said: They are the emirs.
So these are two views.
The third view: Ibn Jurayj said: It is like His saying ﴿عَنِ اليَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾: the one on the right writes the good deeds, and the one on the left writes the bad deeds.
And ﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ﴾ means they record against him his speech and his deeds.
The most fitting of these views is the first, because of the high standing and soundness of its chain of transmission.
It is strengthened by the fact that Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Abū l-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has angels who take turns among you by night and by day…" and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
And Shuʿba narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying ﴿إنَّ قُرْآنَ الفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾, that he said: They go round like guards — the angels of the night and the angels of the day.
And Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he recited: ﴿معقِّباتٌ﴾ «من بين يديه ورقباء من خلفه، من أمر الله يحفظونه» ("followers in turn before him and watchers behind him; by Allah's command they guard him").
So this has made the meaning clear.
And al-Ḥasan said concerning the meaning: they guard him by (ʿan) Allah's command. [This is close to the first, i.e. their guarding him is from Allah,] not from themselves.
And ʿAmr ibn Mālik narrated from Abū l-Jawzāʾ regarding His saying ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ.
And by this too he means the angels.
And it is reported from some of them that he recited «معاقيبُ من بين يديه ومن خلفه», and «معاقيب» is the plural of مُعَقِّب; its interpretation is like the interpretation of the first.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَالٍ﴾.
That is, there is no one to take charge of them apart from Allah.
And «وَالٍ» and وليّ are one and the same, just as one says قدير and قادر, and حفيظ and حافظ.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, fear for the traveller and hope for the one at home.
The meaning is that the traveller fears the rain and is harmed by it.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ﴾.
And the one at home is the one who benefits from the rain; he hopes for it when he sees the lightning.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُنْشِىءُ ٱلسَّحَابَ ٱلثِّقَالَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Those in which there is rain.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Sālim, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: The thunder (al-raʿd) is an angel who glorifies.
And ʿUthmān ibn al-Aswad narrated from Mujāhid, who said: The thunder is an angel named "al-Raʿd." Do you not hear His saying: ﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾?
And Sufyān narrated from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, from Mujāhid, who said: The thunder is an angel who drives the clouds with his voice.
ʿIkrima said: The thunder is an angel who calls out to the clouds as the camel-driver calls out to the camels.
And it is narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās, when he heard the sound of thunder, used to say: "Glory be to the One for whom you have glorified."
And Mālik narrated from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, that when he heard the sound of thunder he would leave off his talk and say: "Glory be to the One whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him," then he would say: This is a severe warning to the people of the earth.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلصَّوَاعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It is possible that the wāw is a wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He strikes with them whom He wills while he is in the state of disputing.
For it is narrated that Arbad asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: Tell us about our Lord — is He of copper or of iron? So Allah sent a thunderbolt which killed him.
And it is possible that His saying ﴿وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾ is cut off from (i.e. independent of) what precedes.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْمِحَالِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, al-ḥawl (might).
Qatāda said: That is, al-ḥīla (stratagem).
Al-Ḥasan said: al-makr (devising/plotting).
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: That is, destruction.
These are views close to one another, and the one most resembling the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that it is destruction (al-ihlāk), because al-maḥl is severity, so it is as if the meaning were: severe in punishment and destruction.
A group of the people of language, among them "Abū ʿUbayda" and "Abū ʿUbayd," said: It is plotting (al-makr), from their saying مَحَلَ به ("he plotted against him"), and he recited the verse of al-Aʿshā:
فَرْعُ نَبْعٍ يَهْتَزُّ فِي غُصُنِ المَجْدِ * غَزِيرُ النَّدَى شَدِيدُ المِحَالِ.
(A branch of the nabʿ tree swaying on the bough of glory, abundant in generosity, severe in cunning/might.)
Abū ʿUbayd said: What best fits the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās is that he read «شديد المَحَال» with fatḥa on the mīm.
As for al-Aʿraj, what is known of his reading is «المَحَال» with fatḥa on the mīm.
And its meaning is like the meaning of al-ḥawl in their saying: لا حَوْلَ وَلاَ قوَّةَ إلاَّ باللهِ ("there is no might and no power except through Allah").
As for the meaning of plotting (makr) on the part of Allah: it is bringing what is hateful upon the one who deserves it from where he does not perceive.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There is no god but Allah."
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said likewise.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لاَ يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيْءٍ إِلاَّ كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, he points to the water with his hand and calls it with his tongue.
Others said: That is, the one who calls upon idols is like one who grasps at water: nothing is gained by him.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَللَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً﴾.
It was said: whoever embraced Islam willingly, and whoever did not embrace Islam until his head was searched out by the sword, so that his entry was at first unwilling.
And it was said: this applies universally, because everyone who worships other than Allah only directs himself to what is great in his heart, and Allah is the Great, the Most Great.
Prostration (al-sujūd) in the language is submission and yielding, and there is nothing but that it submits to Allah and yields to Him.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَظِلالُهُم بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾.
It is narrated that the unbeliever prostrates to other than Allah while his shadow prostrates to Allah, and this is of yielding and submission.
And it was said: the shadows (al-ẓilāl) here are the persons (bodies).

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ جَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ ٱلْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
That is, have they seen anyone other than Allah create the like of His creation, so that the creation became confusingly alike to them?!

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَنَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Kathīr informed me, saying: I heard Mujāhid say: according to the measure of their filling.
Ibn Jurayj said: according to their smallness and their largeness.
Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read ﴿فَسَالَتْ أوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدْرِهَا﴾ (with sukūn on the dāl), and the meaning is the same.
And it was said: its meaning is "according to what was measured out for them."
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱحْتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيْلُ زَبَداً رَّابِياً﴾.
That is, rising up, high.
Mujāhid said: The statement is complete (here).
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلنَّارِ ٱبْتِغَآءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِّثْلُهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The goods (al-matāʿ) are iron, copper and lead.
Others said: That which is heated in pursuit of ornament is gold and silver.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, as solidified (residue).
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: One says أجفأَتِ القِدْرُ ("the pot cast off its froth") when it boils until its froth runs out, and when it solidifies at its bottom.
Abū Zayd said: Ruʾba used to read ﴿فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَالاً﴾; one says جَفَلتِ الرِّيحُ السَّحَابَ when the wind breaks up the clouds and carries them off.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is the water, and this is a parable of truth and falsehood; i.e. the truth remains and is benefited from, and falsehood goes away and vanishes, just as this froth goes away, and like the going away of the dross of these things.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلأَمْثَالَ﴾.
The statement is complete (here).

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
Qatāda said: It is Paradise.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوۤءُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
Abū l-Jawzāʾ said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: meaning the close scrutiny of deeds.
This is indicated by the ḥadīth: "Whoever has his reckoning scrutinised is ruined."
Farqad said: Ibrāhīm said to me: O Farqad, do you know what the evil reckoning is? I said: No. He said: That the servant is taken to account for all of his sins, and nothing of them is forgiven him.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾.
That is, whoever was righteous.
They do not enter it by lineage.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ﴾.
That is, as an honour from Allah to them.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ﴾.
That is, they say: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَىٰ ٱلدَّارِ﴾.
Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī said: ﴿فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّار﴾ — Paradise in place of the Fire.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ مَتَاعٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it passes away.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِيۤ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ﴾.
أناب (anāba): when he returns to obedience.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, by affirming His oneness and by praising Him.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَلاَ بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ﴾.
That is, those which are the hearts of the believers.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Umāma said: «طُوبَى» is a tree in Paradise.
ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said likewise.
Mujāhid said: It is Paradise.
ʿIkrima said: That is, how excellent is what they have!
Ibrāhīm said: «طُوبَى» means good and honour.
These views are close to one another, because «طُوبَى» is of the pattern fuʿlā from al-ṭīb (goodness), i.e. of the good life for them, and these things all go back to the good thing.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, a place of return.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The unbelievers said to the Prophet ﷺ: Make the mountains move for us, cut the earth apart for us, bring the dead to life for us.
Mujāhid said: They said to the Prophet ﷺ: Move these mountains away from us, and pray for us that we may have crops, and bring Syria close to us, for we trade there, and bring the dead to life for us.
Qatāda said: Quraysh said to the Prophet: Bring the dead to life for us, so that we may ask them about what you have brought — is it true? So Allah sent down ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
He said: If this had been done for the People of the Book, it would have been done for you.
All these views require that the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, because the hearer knows it; for they asked, and their asking was an indication of the apodosis of (لو).
Its parallel is: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أوْ آوِي إلَى رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾.
And the poet said:
فَلَوْ أنَّها نَفْسٌ تَمُوتُ سَوِيَّةً * وَلَكِنَّهَا نَفْسٌ تَسَاقَطُ أنْفُسَا
(If it were a soul that died all at once… but it is a soul that falls away soul by soul.)
So the apodosis of (لو) is omitted, i.e. "it would have found consolation."
Concerning what is omitted from the verse there are two views:
Most of the people of language hold that the meaning is: and if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were moved, or the earth cut apart, or the dead spoken to, it would be this Qurʾān.
Some of them said: the meaning is: if this were done for them, they still would not believe, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَا إلَيْهِمْ المَلاَئِكَةَ، وَكَلَّمَهُمُ المَوْتَى، وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلاً، مَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إلاَّ أنْ يَشَاءَ اللهُ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: [And it was said: in the statement there is] fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), and the meaning is: and they disbelieve in the All-Merciful even if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were moved; i.e. they would disbelieve even if this happened.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَى ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is much disagreement concerning this verse.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, and ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read ﴿أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّن الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — abridged. [Translator's note: the word «مختصر» ("abridged") stands as written in the source; the chain is also given as written, though it is usually "Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm from ʿIkrima".]
And in the book of Khārija, Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّنْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾.
And al-Minhāl ibn ʿUmayr narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾, i.e. "have they not known?"
Most of the people of language hold this view.
Among those who held it were Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda. Suḥaym ibn Wuthayl said:
أقُولُ لَهُمْ بِالشِّعْبِ إذْ يَيْسِرُونَنِي * ألَمْ تَيْأَسُوا أنِّي ابنُ فَارِسِ زَهْدَمِ
(I say to them in the mountain pass while they are dividing me up by lot: Do you not know that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam?)
And it is also narrated: إذْ يأسِرونني ("while they are taking me captive").
So the meaning of ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾ is: have they not known?
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾ — he said: have they not known? [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «معاوية بن صالح بن علي بن أبي طلحة», evidently for "Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa".]
There is another view on the verse:
Al-Kisāʾī said: I do not know this usage, nor have I heard anyone say يئستُ meaning "I knew"; rather, in my view it is from despair (al-yaʾs) itself. The meaning is: when the unbelievers asked for the mountains to be moved by the Qurʾān, the earth to be cut apart and the dead to be spoken to, the believers became eager for that and hoped that the unbelievers would be given it and so would believe. So Allah said: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾, i.e. have those who believe not despaired of the faith of these people, because they know that if Allah wished to guide them He would have guided them — as you say: "I have despaired of so-and-so ever succeeding," meaning: because of what I know of him.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ تُصِيبُهُم بِمَا صَنَعُواْ قَارِعَةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Meaning the raiding parties (al-sarāyā).
ʿIkrima and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said likewise, except that Abū ʿĀṣim narrated from Shabīb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the calamity.
Mujāhid said: qāriʿa means a raiding party and a misfortune that befalls them.
Al-qāriʿa in the language is the great misfortune.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيباً مِّن دَارِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: Or you, O Muḥammad, alight near their home.
Saʿīd ibn Mūsā narrated to us in Qarqīsiyā, saying: Makhlad ibn Mālik narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Salama, from Khuṣayf, who said: al-qāriʿa is the raiding parties that the Messenger of Allah used to send out, or you, O Muḥammad, alight near their home.
Al-Ḥasan said: Or the qāriʿa alights near their home.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, the conquest of Mecca.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He is Allah, majestic is His majesty.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means Himself, Mighty and Majestic is He; He is the One who stands over His servants, whoever of them is righteous and whoever of them is wicked, providing for them and feeding them, while they have assigned partners to Allah.
Allah said: ﴿قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ﴾ — and if they named them they would be lying, and would be informing Him of what He does not know; and that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl narrated from al-Khalīl, who said: «مَثَلُ» means "description" (ṣifa). On this basis the meaning is: the description of the Garden that the God-fearing were promised is that rivers flow beneath it — as you say: "the description of so-and-so is: dark-skinned," because its meaning is "so-and-so is dark-skinned."
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: Allah has made a likeness for us of what is unseen by what we see, and such is the speech of the Arabs. So the meaning is: the likeness of the Garden that the God-fearing were promised is a garden beneath which rivers flow.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ مَآبِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, to Him is the destination of every servant.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثْبِتُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿وَيُثَبِّتُ﴾ (with shadda).
It is narrated from him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, settles the affair of the year in the month of Ramaḍān, and He erases what He wills and confirms, except life and death, and wretchedness and happiness.
And in the narration of Abū Ṣāliḥ: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — of what the recording angels have written — whatever is neither for the person nor against him, ﴿وَيُثْبِتُ﴾ what is for him and against him.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾ — he says: Allah replaces of the Qurʾān what He wills and abrogates it, and confirms what He wills and does not replace it.
﴿وَعِندَهُ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ — he says: the whole of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated. Qatāda said likewise.
Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿يَمْحُو اللهُ ما يَشَاءُ﴾ means He abrogates; and it is as though the meaning of ﴿ويُثْبِتُ﴾ in his view is: He does not abrogate it, so it is firmly established (muḥkam).
And «يُثَبِّت» with shadda is for intensity/multiplicity.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «وَيُثْبِت» without shadda is more comprehensive of these views than «يُثَبِّتُ».
Abū ʿUbayd had chosen ﴿وَيُثَبِّتُ﴾, though Abū Ḥātim indicated that their meaning is one.
And ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: He erases whoever's term has come, and confirms whoever's term has not yet come, until his term.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ وَعَلَيْنَا ٱلْحِسَابُ﴾.
That is, whether We show you some of what We promised you — the making of the religion of Islam prevail over all religion — ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ before that, your duty is only to convey to them, and it is for Us to take them to account and requite them for their deeds.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear that what He promised came to be.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
So He said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَأْتِي ٱلأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾.
Islam prevails by taking away what is in the hands of the polytheists and by making the Muslims prevail over them.
There are several views on this verse, and this is the one most resembling the meaning.
Among the evidence for its correctness is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أنَّا نَأْتِي الأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أطْرَافِهَا أفَهُمُ الغَالِبُونَ﴾. This view is the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
Salama ibn Nubayṭ narrated from him that he said, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَأْتِي ٱلأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾: It is what was conquered of their lands.
And ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is the ruin of the earth until it is in one region of it, i.e. until habitation is in one region of it.
And Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid: ﴿نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ — he said: death: the death of the jurists and the scholars.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لاَ مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: There is none to repel His decree.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: there is no one who follows up His judgement with annulment or alteration.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujāhid: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
And Shuʿba said, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ — He is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He.
Sulaymān al-Taymī said: He is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām."
Qatāda said: Among them is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām," for he said: Qurʾān was revealed concerning me; then he recited: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī and ʿIkrima rejected this view.
Al-Shaʿbī said: This verse was revealed before ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām embraced Islam.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima said: This verse was revealed in Mecca, so how could it have been revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām?
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, Allah suffices as witness, and Allah — twice; he holds that (مَنْ) refers back to the name of Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best of what has been said about this verse, for several reasons:
One of them: it is unlikely that Allah would call one of His creatures to witness.
Among them: what al-Shaʿbī and ʿIkrima objected.
Among them: it has been read ﴿وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتَابِ﴾ with kasra on the mīm, the dāl and the ʿayn. This is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, though there is weakness in the narration: Sulaymān ibn al-Arqam narrated it from al-Zuhrī ibn Sālim, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ read (ومِنْ عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ). [Translator's note: «عن الزهري بن سالم» is as written; the chain is presumably "from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father".] And likewise it is narrated of Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that they both read it so.
And there is no disagreement among the exegetes that the meaning is "and from Allah"; so that the meaning of the two readings be one is better.
And Maḥbūb narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī that he read: {وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ عُلِمَ الكِتَابُ) with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the nominative on «الكتاب».
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of those who said it is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām" and others is also possible, because when the proofs are sound and those who have read the scriptures revealed before the Qurʾān recognise them, it is a confirmed matter.
And Allah knows best the truth of that.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤمۤر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
This is the end of the statement (tamām al-kalām).
And whoever holds that each of these letters conveys a meaning says: the meaning is "I am Allah; I see (anā Allāhu arā)."

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا﴾.
The meaning: you see them without pillars.
And the pronoun may refer back to the pillars [i.e. without pillars that you can see].
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ﴾.
That is, they are both subdued and governed; this is the meaning of taskhīr in the language.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
That is, He spread it out.
﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ﴾, i.e. mountains.
﴿وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَاتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, i.e. two kinds; and every kind is a zawj (pair-member).

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ﴾.
There are two views on this:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means the good [soil] and the bad, the salty marshes and the sweet.
And Mujāhid said the same.
The other view: that there is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech, and the meaning is: and in the earth are neighbouring tracts and non-neighbouring ones; just as He said ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تقيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾, where the meaning is "and protect you from the cold", and that was omitted because the listener knows it.
﴿المُتَجَاوِرَاتُ﴾ are the cities and what is inhabited, and ﴿وغَيْرَ مُتَجَاوِرَاتٍ﴾ are the deserts and what is uninhabited.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾.
That is, and in it are gardens of grapevines.
﴿وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ﴾.
Abū Rajāʾ, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read ﴿صُنْوَانٌ﴾ with ḍamma on the ṣād.
Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Barāʾ, who said: «الصنوان» is [palms] growing together, and "not «صنوان»" is those growing separately.
Zuhayr ibn Sharīk narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya narrated to us: Abū Isḥāq said, from al-Barāʾ, concerning His saying ﴿صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ﴾: he said: «الصنوان» is what has a single root while being separate [above], and "not «صنوان»" is what grows alone. [Translator's note: the source prints «أصلحه», evidently for «أصله» (its root); translated accordingly.]
And so it is in the language: a palm tree that has another palm or more [growing from it] is called "«صنوان»", and when they are separate it is said: "not «صنوان»".
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُسْقَىٰ بِمَآءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي ٱلأُكُلِ﴾.
That is, in fruit; i.e. they come out different, even though the air is one. So it is known that this is not because of the air, nor of nature, and that they have a Governor.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي ٱلأُكُلِ﴾. He said: The sweet, the sour, the Persian [dates] and the poor-quality dates (al-daqal).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإِن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾.
That is, if you wonder at their denial of the resurrection after these proofs, then that is indeed something that ought to be wondered at.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: [They ask you to hasten] punishment before well-being.
Someone else said: He means their saying: ﴿اللهُمَّ إنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ ٱلْمَثُلاَتُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the examples (al-amthāl).
Qatāda said: He means the exemplary punishments.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is more fitting, because it is well known in the language that a severe punishment is called mathula and muthla.
It is narrated from al-Aʿmash that he read ﴿المُثُلاَتُ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and the thāʾ. This too is the plural of (مُثْلة).
And it is narrated from him that he read ﴿المُثْلاَتُ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ.
This too is the plural of (مُثْلة).
And (المُثْلاَتُ) [i.e. al-muthalāt] is permissible, a fatḥa being substituted for the ḍamma because of its heaviness.
It is also said: The fatḥa comes as a compensation for the hāʾ [of the feminine].
And it is also narrated from al-Aʿmash that he read ﴿المثْلاَتُ﴾ with fatḥa on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ; this is the plural of (مَثْلَة) — then the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness.
[Translator's note: the vowel signs in this passage are printed as given; the forms described in words (muthulāt, muthlāt, muthalāt, mathlāt) do not always match the vocalisation printed in the parentheses.]
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ﴾.
Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ﴾ was revealed, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Were it not for Allah's pardon, His mercy and His overlooking, no one's life would be pleasant; and were it not for His punishment, His threat and His chastisement, everyone would rely [on His forgiveness and neglect to act]."

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said — and this is the sense of their words: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ means the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾, i.e. a prophet who calls them.
Sufyān narrated from Abū al-Ḍuḥā: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ — he said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ [— he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: The meaning is: for every people there is] a caller to guidance or a caller to misguidance.
What a group of the lexicographers hold is that the meaning is: when they demanded signs, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that every people has a prophet who guides them and makes things clear to them, and that it is not incumbent on him to bring them whatever signs they demand.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ — he said: Allah, exalted be His mention.
Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿اللهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِل كُلُّ أُنْثَى﴾. Sufyān said: He means whether male or female.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the child's falling short of nine months, and its exceeding them.
Qatāda said: [The wombs] fall short with the miscarried foetus, and exceed beyond the nine months.
Mujāhid said: Al-ghayḍ is decrease. When a woman sheds blood while pregnant, the child is diminished; and when she does not shed blood, the child grows large and complete.
[Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: When a woman becomes pregnant and then menstruates,] her child is diminished; then the pregnancy is lengthened for it by the amount [of time] the blood came to her.
ʿIkrima said: Al-ghayḍ is that the child is diminished by the coming of the blood, and the increase is that [the pregnancy] increases by the amount [of days] during which the blood came to her, until she completes nine months, apart from the days during which the blood came to her.
